items.evidence: customer-note.spec.ts:173-176 reloads the page and asserts noteInput toHaveValue(note), after a guard at :154 that the seeded note is empty. If the save mutation never ran, the reload would show an empty note.
Runs as actor 'customer' (:126, user.manager@example.com, MANAGE_USERS only). The note value is asserted after saving (:169) and again after a reload (:176).
No existing page object covers the Customers list or customer details screens, and no helper or constant is duplicated: CUSTOMER and ORDERS_SCENARIO are imported from scenarios/orders.ts.
No waitForTimeout or sleeps. Every wait is on a named UI state: toast, href, URL, row count.
Imports test from fixtures/test.ts, is not tagged parallel(), and writes nothing to the cache, dumps or sessions.

Uses data-test-id and role locators throughout. The coordinate hover in customerListPage.ts:102 is forced by the canvas grid, which has no DOM rows; the click itself goes through the test-id anchor, and its href is checked first.
No data is created or changed in the spec. The customer comes from ORDERS_SCENARIO, and the spec reaches her through the list search.
No hard-coded ids; the customer is found by search on CUSTOMER.email. Assertions use CUSTOMER constants, not populatedb values.
Uses test.use({ actor: "customer" }) with no UI login and no credentials in the spec.
typecheck.txt reports exit 0, and the spec lives in e2e/tests/customers/.
The spec defines no locators; all of them are on CustomerListPage and CustomerDetailsPage.
Both page objects use readonly fields initialised from this.page and constructor(readonly page: Page) {}.
Has // Arrange (:130) and // Act & Assert (:136), which matches the suite's pattern.
One test with a test.step for each of its four stages.
Title 'Customer manager saves a note on a customer #e2e' says what is checked and carries the #e2e tag.
The header comment at :119-125 says what the spec covers and why the customer is reached by search.
All assertions are web-first expect(locator) calls.
Expected values come from CUSTOMER and ORDERS_SCENARIO. The note literal is test input, not a scenario value.
No cleanup code and no unique names; the comment notes the fixed note is fine because the database is reset.
No per-test timeouts, retries, networkidle or waitForLoadState.
Relative imports keep .ts. The spec takes test and expect only from the fixture; page objects import expect from @playwright/test, as draftOrderPage.ts does.
No any, no casts and no gql calls.
Comments explain reasons (the empty-note guard, the canvas grid geometry, the hover/href wait, the skeleton on reload) rather than narrating.

structured_output.summary: Submission c18bb572 meets all 23 checklist items. The test runs as the MANAGE_USERS-only "customer" actor on ORDERS_SCENARIO and finds Ada Lovelace through the list search, so it needs no hard-coded id. It checks the note is empty before writing, saves through new page objects, and confirms the note is still there after a reload. That reload check is what proves the save reached the server. The type check passes (exit 0). The one fragile part is the fixed-coordinate hover used to open a row in the canvas grid (customerListPage.ts:102). I did not fail B6 for it because the grid has no DOM rows to locate, and the code checks the anchor's href before clicking.
